key_insight: Self-distillation does not reliably improve reasoning; the paper finds that apparent gains often come from overfitting or reusing existing behavior rather than effectively leveraging privileged information.
engineering_relevance: For practitioners building reasoning models, this suggests self-distillation should be treated as a risky optimization strategy that may not translate to robust out-of-distribution gains without stronger evaluation and reward-aligned training.
method: Revisit two self-distillation methods: SDPO and OPSD.
Test across code, science, tool use, and math reasoning tasks.
Compare self-distillation gradients with policy gradients for reward optimization.
evidence_signal: The authors evaluate Qwen3 models from 1.7B to 14B parameters and OLMo-3-7B, finding that reported improvements do not consistently generalize to unseen problems.
watch_item: Self-distillation may look effective on in-distribution benchmarks while failing to provide a policy-improving gradient direction, so generalization and gradient alignment should be checked carefully.
